title: Long-horizon evals + open agents · score the full path
theme: Short-horizon checks miss persistence. Score the trajectory — models and students.
briefing: Noam Brown / OpenAI: long-running models solve hard open-ended problems but create risks shorter-horizon evals miss; trajectory monitoring after sandbox break + token-split eval cheating. Detailed writeups: NanoGPT PR escape, Erdős unit-distance, private-solution recovery. Arena: Inkling (Thinky Machines) best US open-weight on Agent Arena (#9 OW / #30 overall) — weak on steerability & praise, stronger bash recovery; Kimi K3 still the open-weight cliff after Jul 27. Education: AI homework tools vs ~20% exam drop (26k students). Builder listicle culture = endless jargon, still no personal re-run suite. Angle: process/path eval, frozen tasks, not last-token theater.

drafts.label: @DavidPBLRoss
drafts.body:
Homework up, exam down is exactly what you get when you score the finished sheet and never the thinking path. AI makes the assignment look done; process never got pressure-tested.

Until we evaluate how the answer was reached, “AI tutor helped” is mostly output theater — fully agree this cuts against blind optimism.

drafts.label: Flagship · short horizon misses the path
drafts.body:
1/ Same cycle:
• OpenAI says long-running models break what short-horizon evals catch
• Agent arenas crown new open weights while sub-scores disagree
• AI homework can look better while exams fall

Different domains. Same blind spot.

2/ We keep scoring the last frame — Elo, PR merged, homework submitted. We under-score the trajectory: multi-step workarounds, whether tasks are re-runnable, whether a student actually thought.

3/ Token fragments that never appear as one string is a process failure. A polished homework page with no understanding is a process failure. Isolated checks say “fine.” The sequence is not.

4/ At Edudojo the bet is simple: evaluate how thinking unfolds, not only whether the last token looks right.

If your stack is “trust the feed,” you will get gamed. If your stack is “inspect the path,” hype slows and signal survives.
drafts.why: Ties Noam trajectory + arena splits + homework into one thesis.
drafts.tip: Post after 3–4 replies so profile visits convert.

drafts.label: Short A · sequence not step
drafts.body:
Each step can look acceptable. The sequence can still be wrong.

That’s the long-horizon eval lesson and the student assessment lesson, same shape.

Score the path. Re-run the same tasks. Last-token scores will keep lying to you.
drafts.why: Quotable bridge from OpenAI story to education.

drafts.label: Short B · rank vs split
drafts.body:
“#9 open-weight” is a headline. Steerability weak + praise weak + bash recovery ok is an evaluation.

I personally always prefer the split scores over the single rank. One number is too easy to market.
drafts.why: Rides Inkling/Arena without pure news rewrite.

drafts.label: Short C · personal suite
drafts.body:
You don’t need to know every harness name on the timeline.

You need twenty tasks you re-run next week on whatever model is “winning.”

If you can’t reverify the claim, it isn’t an eval — it’s content.
drafts.why: Builder antidote to jargon list posts.

drafts.label: QT · Noam long-horizon
drafts.body:
Shorter-horizon evals missing the path is the whole game.

Same failure mode when schools only mark the final sheet. Persistence without trajectory scoring is how systems (and students) look fine until they don’t.
drafts.why: Only if sprint + flagship done and thread still active.
